source.version: Published proceedings paper, Proceedings of the 59th Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences, 2026, printed pp. 95-103 (PDF pp. 1-9).
source.title_on_document: The Confidence Cage: How Creative Self-Efficacy Hinders Gen AI-Augmented Ideation

supplement.holds: No supplementary material or online appendix is referenced. The saved PDF contains the article and references, with no appendix; no statistics are identified as residing in a supplement.

paper_design_summary: Prolific participants completed a fork Alternative Uses Test before being randomly assigned to a GPT-4o chatbot coach or a text-only web-search tool for a Frisbee Alternative Uses Test in the same online session. The final analyzed sample comprised 300 people, 150 per condition; the tools were available during the scored post-test task (PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Sections 3.1-3.2). Responses received an automated composite creativity score, while ideation and baseline creative self-efficacy were self-reports (PDF pp. 4-5 [printed pp. 98-99], Section 3.3).

studies.label: Online pre-test/post-test Alternative Uses Test experiment

assignment.what_was_assigned: Participants were assigned to Human-AI or Human-Search for the post-test Frisbee task after completing the pre-test fork task. Condition was between participants and time was within participants (PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Sections 3.1-3.2).
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions for the post-test task with control.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Sections 3.1 Design and participants and 3.2 Procedure

arms.name: Human-AI
arms.description: Custom GPT-4o chatbot available during the Frisbee post-test, asking probing questions and offering new perspectives without direct solutions. Participants were instructed to use it as a collaborative thinking tool; copy-paste was disabled (PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Section 3.2).

arms.name: Human-Search
arms.description: Custom text-only search engine available during the Frisbee post-test. Participants were instructed to use it for inspiration rather than direct answers and had the same copy-paste restriction (PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Section 3.2).

participants.exclusions: 327 people were recruited, and 27 were excluded from analyses: copying complete responses verbatim from internet resources (n = 15), failure to follow task instructions (n = 8), incomplete task completion (n = 3), or chatbot system error (n = 1). The final analyzed sample was 300, with 150 per arm. The paper does not state a total or arm counts at random assignment before exclusions, nor exclusions by arm; 327 is a recruited count, not a confirmed randomized count (PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Section 3.1).
participants.who: Recruited through Prolific; required to be at least 18 years old, fluent in English, and currently residing in the United States or Canada (PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Section 3.1).
participants.quote: The final sample included 300 participants, with 150 assigned to each experimental condition.
participants.locator: PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Section 3.1; PDF p. 6 [printed p. 100], Table 2, n column

ai_tool.name_model: Custom chatbot powered by OpenAI's GPT-4o API
ai_tool.how_used: Available during the post-test as a brainstorming partner that asked probing questions and offered new perspectives without supplying direct task solutions. Copy-paste was disabled, and instructions framed the chatbot as a collaborative thinking tool (PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Section 3.2).

task.description: Guilford Alternative Uses Test: generate as many creative and unusual uses as possible for a fork at pre-test, then for a Frisbee at post-test. Instructions emphasized novel and practical uses. The assigned AI or search aid was available for the Frisbee task (PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Sections 3.2-3.3).
task.duration: 5 minutes per AUT task; approximately 25-30 minutes for the online experiment (PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Section 3.2).

outcomes.name: Post-test composite creativity score on Frisbee alternative uses
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: An LLM-based automated system evaluates novelty, usefulness, and divergence from typical applications and produces a composite creativity score, citing Organisciak et al. (2023). Separate component scores are not reported, and the exact scoring model, scale anchors, and aggregation across each participant's responses are not specified (PDF pp. 4-5 [printed pp. 98-99], Section 3.3). The analysis uses participant creativity scores. H1 is tested by ANCOVA adjusting for pre-test creativity, age, work experience, gender, and race; unadjusted descriptive scores and path/mediation estimates concern this same output outcome (PDF p. 5 [printed p. 99], Sections 3.4 and 4; PDF p. 6 [printed p. 100], Tables 2-3). The indirect effects use self-reported ideation as mediator, with 5,000 bootstrap samples and 95% bias-corrected confidence intervals (PDF p. 5 [printed p. 99], Section 3.4). This is the sole scored creativity outcome, but no explicit primary-outcome designation is stated.

contrasts.reported: Table 2 unadjusted post-test scores: Human-AI M = 3.21, SD = 0.22, n = 150; Human-Search M = 2.98, SD = 0.31, n = 150. Pre-test scores: Human-AI M = 2.94, SD = 0.37; Human-Search M = 2.85, SD = 0.38. Section 4 ANCOVA: F(1, 293) = 58.28, p < .001, partial eta-squared = .166; adjusted Human-AI M = 3.19, SE = 0.02, 95% CI [3.15, 3.24], versus Human-Search M = 2.99, SE = 0.02, 95% CI [2.95, 3.04]; adjusted mean difference = 0.20; Cohen's d = 0.77. IMPORTANT SOURCE DISCREPANCY: Table 2's adjusted post-test column instead prints Human-Search 3.19 [3.15, 3.24] and Human-AI 2.99 [2.95, 3.04], reversing the arm labels relative to Section 4 and Figure 1. Both versions are preserved here; the discrepancy is unresolved. Additional estimates for this same creativity outcome: the condition coefficient in the creativity equation after accounting for ideation is B = 0.169, SE = 0.032, z = 5.25, p < .001, 95% CI [0.110, 0.232]. The indirect effect through ideation is B = 0.031, SE = 0.013, z = 2.38, p = .017, 95% CI [0.010, 0.062]. Conditional indirect effects are B = 0.040, SE = 0.017, 95% CI [0.013, 0.080] at low CSE (-1 SD), B = 0.031, SE = 0.013, 95% CI [0.010, 0.062] at mean CSE, and B = 0.021, SE = 0.010, 95% CI [0.006, 0.050] at high CSE (+1 SD). The index of moderated mediation is B = -0.008, SE = 0.004, z = -2.05, p = .040, 95% CI [-0.021, -0.001]. These direct and indirect effects are distinct from the main ANCOVA total contrast.
contrasts.locator: Unadjusted arm statistics and conflicting adjusted arm labels: PDF p. 6 [printed p. 100], Table 2 (embedded table image). ANCOVA F, partial eta-squared, adjusted means/SEs/CIs, adjusted difference, and d: PDF p. 5 [printed p. 99], Section 4. Figure 1 on PDF p. 6 [printed p. 100] supports the narrative direction. Path and indirect-effect statistics: PDF p. 6 [printed p. 100], Section 4 and Table 3; Table 3 note on PDF p. 7 [printed p. 101].

sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: Not stated; no reuse of another paper's participants is reported. The methods describe recruitment for this experiment.

company_involvement.description: No company authorship, funding, or research partnership is disclosed. All authors are affiliated with Elon University. OpenAI is identified as the provider of the GPT-4o API used for the intervention; Prolific and Qualtrics are named as study platforms.
company_involvement.locator: PDF p. 1 [printed p. 95], author affiliations; PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Sections 3.1-3.2; no company disclosure in the remainder of the PDF.

eligibility.reason: People were randomly assigned to a generative-AI coach or an active web-search comparison during a creative task (PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Sections 3.1-3.2). The final analyzed sample was 300 people, 150 per arm, exceeding the 50-person threshold (PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Section 3.1; PDF p. 6 [printed p. 100], Table 2). The AUT responses received an LLM-based composite creativity score (PDF pp. 4-5 [printed pp. 98-99], Section 3.3). AI was available while the scored post-test output was produced, so this answers with_ai, not after_ai. The adjusted-means discrepancy affects extraction but does not negate these eligibility facts.

one_line_finding: AI coaching improved scored AUT creativity relative to web search (reported adjusted difference = 0.20, Cohen's d = 0.77; PDF p. 5 [printed p. 99], Section 4), but Table 2 reverses the adjusted arm labels (PDF p. 6 [printed p. 100]).
open_questions: Which arm labels are correct for the adjusted means? Section 4 assigns 3.19 to Human-AI and 2.99 to Human-Search; Table 2 prints the opposite labels, while Figure 1 agrees with the narrative direction (PDF pp. 5-6 [printed pp. 99-100]).
What are the total and arm-specific numbers at random assignment, and exclusions by arm? The document provides recruited and final analyzed counts only (PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Section 3.1).

Which LLM/model implementation and scale were used to score the responses, and how were multiple responses combined into each participant's creativity score? These details are not stated in Section 3.3 (PDF pp. 4-5 [printed pp. 98-99]).
What standardizer was used for the reported ANCOVA Cohen's d = 0.77? The effect is printed without a calculation rule (PDF p. 5 [printed p. 99], Sections 3.4 and 4).
notes: Screened from the complete markdown and all pages of the saved PDF. No appendix is present. PDF page numbers are given alongside printed proceedings page numbers. Tables 1 and 2 and Figures 1 and 2 are embedded images and were inspected directly from the PDF in memory; Table 3 was checked with PDF text extraction and table recovery. No effect sizes were calculated. Only the output-scored composite creativity measure is listed as an outcome. The Runco Ideational Behavior Scale mediator and baseline creative self-efficacy are self-reports, not scored creative outputs (PDF p. 5 [printed p. 99], Section 3.3). The paper reports no across-person diversity outcome or creative task after AI withdrawal. Baseline fork scores are covariates/descriptive pre-test values, not a separate after_ai outcome. Participant-level counts are in participants and arms; n_units is left null because the analysis unit is participant. No preregistration, data URL, code URL, or supplementary material is stated.
